Visa's detailed onboarding standard is public: the Visa Acceptance Risk Standards of October 2024, marked 'Visa Public', replaced the Global Acquirer Risk Standards and were on usa.visa.com on 4 October 2026 (latest version: Visa's client portal). Their mandatory know-your-customer controls make the acquirer collect the merchant's trading and legal name, outlet address, telephone and business registration or tax number; each principal's or director's name, address, government ID number, email and telephone; ownership percentages; a business licence or registration certificate; screen sanctions lists; and, for e-commerce, list the merchant's URLs and verify that it owns the domains.583

Source trap

Strong customer authentication (SCA) has one legal date: 14 September 2019 (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/389). 31 December 2020 is from an EBA Opinion of 16 October 2019 on when migration plans for e-commerce card payments 'should be completed'. On 24 December 2019 the CBC said it did not intend to take supervisory enforcement action against licensed institutions without SCA in remote electronic card transactions by then, if they had submitted a migration plan; 14 September 2019 'remains as the legal deadline'.273274276

Not established in this section

  • Deposit guarantee and safeguarding accounts. Are the customers of an e-money or payment institution covered by look-through when its safeguarding account sits at a Cyprus bank? look again by 4 Apr 2027
  • Card-acceptance duty: enforcement figures and later decrees. How many inspections and fines has the card-acceptance duty produced, and has any decree or technical link followed K.D.P. 248/2022? look again by 4 Jan 2027
  • Surcharge ban: how art. 62(5) is read. Has any authority or court applied art. 62(5) of Law 31(I)/2018, in particular to commercial or three-party cards? look again by 4 Apr 2027
  • PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation. Have the two acts been adopted, and from when would they apply? look again by 14 Dec 2026

What is known on each point, and where it was looked for, is in the register at the end.

Question 5, continued · What the card schemes and PCI ask

What Visa, Mastercard and PCI ask: registration, thresholds, disputes, questionnaires, interchange

The schemes bind the acquirer, which passes the duties on by contract. Visa prints its high-risk categories and monitoring thresholds; Mastercard stopped printing its chargeback thresholds by 2021. Interchange is 0.20% and 0.30% on EEA consumer cards and mostly 1.3% to 2.0% on commercial cards; neither scheme's European fee page publishes scheme fees.

Visa and Mastercard each require the acquirer to hold an agreement with every merchant it acquires from; where a registered payment facilitator stands between them, the facilitator holds the agreement with each sponsored merchant. The duties below are written for the acquirer and reach the merchant through that agreement. Read here: Visa's Core Rules of 18 April 2026 and, in Internet Archive captures, Mastercard's Rules of 2 June 2026, its Security Rules and Procedures - Merchant Edition of 4 August 2026 and its Chargeback Guide of 19 May 2026.200201581584

Question 6 · Taxes

From 2026: 15% corporate tax, 5% defence contribution on dividends, no stamp duty

The reform in force since 1 January 2026 raised corporate income tax from 12.5% to 15%, cut the special defence contribution (SDC) on dividends to 5% for resident, domiciled individuals, with a 17% transitional rule, and repealed stamp duty. A company pays corporate tax and payroll contributions; a sole trader the personal scale and 16.6% social insurance.

The reform is six tax laws in Official Gazette No. 5070 of 31 December 2025: Laws 239(I)/2025, 241(I)/2025, 242(I)/2025, 243(I)/2025, 244(I)/2025 and 245(I)/2025. They took effect on 1 January 2026; a few provisions apply from tax year 2026, from 1 July 2026 or from 1 January 2031.610

Receipts, invoices and records: the duties and their sanctions

DutyRuleBasis, dates and sanction
Legal receiptA taxable person making a taxable supply to a non-taxable person in Cyprus issues and delivers at that time a receipt showing at least: date; number; supplier's name, address and VAT number; description; total including VAT; per VAT rate the total and the rate; whether the sale is for cash, an advance or part payment.Reg. 13A of K.D.P. 314/2001, applied from 16 January 2012. VAT Law: a charge equal to 20% of the value of the transaction (art. 45(9); 'up to' 20% on the Tax Department's page) and, on conviction, a fine of up to €1,700, imprisonment of up to three years, or both (art. 46(11A)).490496627
Tax invoicesA retailer need not give a VAT invoice unless a taxable customer asks; up to €85, for a customer not in another Member State, a simplified invoice suffices; otherwise a full one. An electronic invoice needs the customer's acceptance. Invoices are issued within 30 days of the transaction, unless the Commissioner allows longer.Regs 11-12, 11A and 14 of K.D.P. 314/2001; art. 30(6) of Law 4/1978. Per the Tax Department's leaflet of June 2017, issuing invoices and receipts electronically requires an approved fiscal device; K.D.P. 29/1997 governs handwritten ones.491628

Unfiled returns (omissions from 1 January 2027): at least two tax returns, twelve monthly withholding returns or three VAT returns. Three notices first: two giving at least ten days each to comply, a third five days for written views. A further 20 days may follow.497
RecordsVAT: six years, unless the Commissioner provides otherwise. How a merchant may be paid, and with whom he may contract

  • Card acceptance: payees contract with lawfully licensed payment service providers within the meaning of Law 31(I)/2018. For card acceptance, and for collection on behalf of a third party generally, they may not contract with entities that are not such providers or their agents, unless legislation expressly provides otherwise (art. 30A(2) of Law 4/1978, in force since 20 August 2020).206
  • Decree K.D.P. 259/2021 repeats the rule, and breaches of the decree are finable under art. 50ΣΤ. The text does not mention payment facilitators.206
  • Cash: persons trading in goods or providing services may receive or pay cash only up to EUR 10,000, in one or more linked operations (art. 2B of AML Law 188(I)/2007, in force since 31 December 2024). Exempt: payments between natural persons not acting professionally; payments, deposits and loan repayments at credit institutions, e-money issuers and payment service providers; casino customers (Law 35(I)/2025).562

Cyprus's non-domicile regime survived the 2026 reform. Among individuals, SDC is charged only on those who are both tax resident and domiciled in Cyprus; an individual tax resident for at least 17 of the last 20 years before the tax year is deemed domiciled. A non-domiciled resident is outside SDC, while the 2.65% GeSY contribution of an income earner covers dividends with no domicile test. Since 1 January 2026 a person without a Cyprus domicile of origin who has become deemed-domiciled may opt, irrevocably, for a flat SDC of €50,000 a year, paid as a single €250,000 instalment per five-year period, for up to two periods.658659

Also changed by Law 245(I)/2025: SDC on rent and interest

SinceWasNowAct
1 Jan 2026SDC on rental income: 3% of gross rents reduced by 25%, in effect 2.25% of gross rent, payable by a person resident in Cyprus (art. 3(2)(δ) of Law 117(I)/2002, in force 1 January 2003; the clause reads the same in the 2002 Gazette text and in archived consolidations up to 7 November 2025). Under art. 4 as archived on 7 November 2025, a tenant that was a company, partnership, the State or a local authority withheld it and paid by 30 June and 31 December; otherwise the landlord paid on the same dates.Abolished from 1 January 2026: Law 245(I)/2025 deleted the rent-related definitions, and the Tax Department's March 2026 presentation lists 'abolition from 1/1/2026 of SDC on rental income'. The GeSY contribution on such income is a separate charge. Interest received by a resident-and-domiciled individual bears 17% under new art. 3B (3% on government savings certificates and bonds and on corporate bonds listed on a recognised stock exchange).Law 245(I)/2025, arts 3 and 4660661

Payments from a Cyprus company to recipients abroad

PaymentRuleBasis and dates
DividendsNo general withholding. SDC reaches only a non-resident company, or a permanent establishment kept there, resident or registered in a low-tax jurisdiction (5%) or an EU-listed non-cooperative jurisdiction (17%; 17% if both), and only where payer and recipient are linked by more than 50% of votes, capital or profit rights.Art. 3(1)(δ) of Law 117(I)/2002 as replaced by Law 245(I)/2025, in force 1 January 2026. InterestA company resident or registered in an EU-listed non-cooperative jurisdiction bears 17% on Cyprus-source interest received or credited, 'whether or not paid', if linked by more than 50% with the paying Cyprus company. Excluded: interest paid by an individual and, if the payer cannot reasonably know, on listed securities.Art. 3B(γ) of Law 117(I)/2002, read 5 October 2026. Three income tax reliefs for a person taking up employment in Cyprus sit in art. 8 of Income Tax Law 118(I)/2002 (read 4 and 5 October 2026). Under (23Α), 50% of remuneration from employment in Cyprus is exempt for 17 tax years, for a person not resident in Cyprus for at least 15 consecutive years before first employment starting on or after 1 January 2022, in any year remuneration exceeds €55,000. Under (21Α), 20% of remuneration or €8,550, whichever is lower, is exempt for seven tax years, for first employment starting up to 2027 after three years' employment abroad by a non-resident employer. These two cannot be combined. A third relief, (21B), was added by Law 17(I)/2026.673674

The first-employment reliefs when the employer is the founder's own company

PointRuleInstrument, dates and limits
The third relief: 25%, art. 8(21B)25% of pay from employment in Cyprus, or of an individual's business profits there, is exempt up to €25,000 a year, in the start year and the six following, each year the income exceeds €30,000. It excludes art. 8(21A) and is excluded by art. 8(23A).Law 17(I)/2026 (Gazette 6 March 2026, deemed in force 1 January 2025). Only for a person who starts in 2025-2030, was not resident in the seven tax years before the start year but was resident in an earlier year, and worked full time abroad for a non-resident employer for 84 months, or 36 of the last 84 with a recognised degree.674
'First employment'Under art. 8(23A), proviso (iv), it starts when a person, after 15 consecutive tax years without any salaried services in Cyprus, begins such services for a resident or non-resident employer. The 50% exemption is anchored to the first employment in Cyprus, not to the founder's own company; art. 8(21A) uses the same definition.Tax Department Circular 4/2024 (8 July 2024): whoever performed salaried services in Cyprus, of any duration, in the 15 tax years before is not eligible (para 10); services count when performed with physical presence in Cyprus (para 11). The Department's FAQ (updated 6 August 2026): changing employer does not affect eligibility.675
A founder already living in CyprusHe may fail the residence test of the 50% exemption. The 15 consecutive years of non-residence are the tax years before the year in which the first employment in Cyprus starts; that year itself is not counted, whether or not the person was resident in it. One earlier year of Cyprus tax residence breaks the chain.Tax Department Circular 4/2024 (8 July 2024), paras 13-14; its example: a start in 2023 requires non-residence in every year from 2008 to 2022. The 20% exemption instead requires three consecutive years of employment outside Cyprus for a non-resident employer immediately before (Circular 10/2022, part II).676
Employment by a company the founder set upThe Tax Department accepts the 50% and 20% exemptions, on conditions: the exemption 'is granted also to persons employed in companies which they themselves or persons connected with them have set up' (Circular 4/2024 of 8 July 2024, para 36, repeating Circular 10/2022 of 1 November 2022).Where the company is dormant, or the size of its activity does not justify the remuneration, or it is not registered as an employer with the Social Insurance Services or in the tax register, or has not filed its employer returns, no salaried services are deemed to exist and neither art. 8(21A) nor art. 8(23A) relief is given.677
A director's fee and the 50% and 20% reliefsThe Tax Department does not count 'gain or profit from holding an office' as remuneration from employment; read plainly, a fee paid to a founder merely as director is outside both reliefs. Pay as Executive Director alongside employment remuneration in Cyprus is counted with it; this bears on the 50% relief's €55,000 threshold.Circular 4/2024, para 11(iii), on art. 8(23A); Circular 10/2022, part I, 1(β)(iii), on arts 8(21A) and 8(23A). Executive Director's pay: under Circular 10/2022 only in the same company or one of the same consolidated group; under Circular 4/2024 in the same or another company, 'connected or not'.678
How a relief is claimedNo application or approval: an eligible taxpayer benefits through his employer's payroll (PAYE) by completing form T.D.59, given to the employer yearly, and must keep evidence — for example foreign payslips, contracts, proof of foreign social insurance, leases, a foreign tax residence certificate for the last 15 years.Tax Department FAQ on art. 8(23A), updated 6 August 2026: as with arts 8(21A) and 8(21B), there is no application-approval procedure. A tax ruling may be requested for the Department's official position. Art. 8(23A) does not cover the self-employed and is independent of non-domicile status: both may be claimed together.679
Form T.D.59 for tax year 2026'Declaration for claiming tax deductions': Part B, line 2, 'deduction for first employment'. Its note 7 offers three options — 20% of remuneration up to €8,550; 50% where the salary exceeds €100,000 (interpretative circular 2017/4); 50% where it exceeds €55,000 'according to circulars 2022/10 and 2024/04'.The employee's social insurance number is a mandatory field. As read on 5 October 2026 no line or note of the form names the 25% relief of art. 8(21B), although the Tax Department's FAQ of 6 August 2026 says that relief too is given without an application.680

Circular 4/2024, Circular 10/2022 and the FAQ are Tax Department texts; the reliefs sit in art. 8 of Law 118(I)/2002.

The founder's own tax file: registration, return, residence certificate, non-domicile forms

PointRuleInstrument, dates and limits
Registration of an individual in the Tax RegisterAn individual gives notice for registration and obtains a tax identification number where he is resident in Cyprus and has reached the age of 25, or has income falling under art. 5 of the Income Tax Law. No period is stated, unlike the 60 days for companies. A founder who draws a salary has such income.S. 5A(1A) of Law 4/1978, inserted by Law 243(I)/2025 (in force 1 January 2026); its proviso — notice until 31 December 2027 for a person with no such income in tax years 2026 and 2027, not yet registered — does not reach him. As of 5 October 2026 the Tax Department accepts the request only through the Tax For All portal.9899
Personal return from tax year 2026Every resident individual aged 25 to 70 at year-end files a return, and one with gross income files at any age. It is due by 31 July of the year after the tax year; a person obliged to prepare audited or reviewed accounts may file by 31 January of the second year. Per the Tax Department it is filed only through Tax For All.Art. 5 of Law 4/1978 as amended by Law 243(I)/2025. The third proviso to s. 5(1) lets the Council of Ministers exempt categories of persons and set criteria under which individuals with gross income within the zero-rate band (€22,000) need not file; the Tax Department's page restates it.58681682
Personal return for tax year 2025Every natural person whose gross income in 2025 does not exceed €19,500 is exempt from filing. The Tax Department reads this as a duty on employees, pensioners and the self-employed above €19,500, filed through TAXISnet by 31 October 2026.Decree K.D.P. 52/2025 (Gazette No. 5928, 21 February 2025); Tax Department announcement of 18 June 2026. The extending decree, K.D.P. 260/2026, does not cover a self-employed person obliged to prepare audited or reviewed accounts. Late filing costs €150 (s. 50A(α) of Law 4/1978, per the announcement).644681
Tax residence certificateAn individual requests it on form T.D.126 (2022), sent by e-mail or letter to the District Tax Office; it costs €80 in fee stamps, paid at collection, and is prepared only where a double tax treaty has been signed with the other country. By its title the form is the declaration 'under the 60-day rule'.Tax Department page updated 28 September 2026: it lists no other form for individuals, does not say what a 183-day resident files and publishes no processing time. For 'foreigners' it names only the 'Yellow Slip' — in common usage the Union citizen's registration certificate — and no residence permit of a third-country national.105106
Non-domicile declaration — form T.D.38 (2016)Non-domicile status is claimed by a declaration the tax office records; the form has no approval step. Per the form, a tax-resident individual files it with the returns section of the office holding his file 'in the first year of acquiring income from dividends / interest / rent' in which he considers himself exempt.Tax Department page (updated 11 September 2026): a 'request for exemption' sent to the District Tax Office, with questionnaires T.D.38ΕρΑ (domicile of origin) and T.D.38ΕρΒ (domicile of choice). Form: he declares under 17 years' residence in the last 20; one without a Cyprus domicile of origin ticks box 2 and attaches T.D.38ΕρΑ.107
Declaration to the paying company — form T.D.624/ΦΠ (2017)With it a non-domiciled shareholder stops his own company from withholding SDC on his dividends. Per the form's notes it is submitted to the organisation that pays the interest, dividends or rent, one form per source of income; the declarant tells the payer in writing within one month if he ceases to qualify.The form's own notes; the payer must let the Commissioner inspect it or hand it over on demand. The Tax Department's domicile page (updated 11 September 2026) lists the form but says of all its forms that they go to the District Tax Office — at odds with the form's note.108
The alternative SDC regime of art. 3Δ of Law 117(I)/2002 — form T.D.631 (2026)A resident without a Cyprus domicile of origin who is about to be deemed domiciled (17 of 20 years) applies on this form. Per its instructions it is signed, scanned and sent as a Tax For All message by 30 June of the first year of the five-year period, or up to two years before the year domicile would be deemed acquired.Listed on the Tax Department's domicile page (updated 11 September 2026) with Circular 02/2026 of 29 May 2026, which was not read. Per the form's instructions the €250,000 for the period is paid by the end of the month after the Commissioner accepts the application.658683

Question 7 · KYC for a person and for a company

KYC: the law says what must be established, each institution publishes its own list or none

Law 188(I)/2007 requires the identity of the customer and the beneficial owner to be verified before a business relationship starts, with derogations. The Central Bank of Cyprus directive in force since 2 June 2025 fixes the data and documents for a person and a company. Published lists differ: some 'ask for', some say 'may be requested', some publish none.

Under art. 61(1) of Law 188(I)/2007 an obliged entity identifies and verifies the customer, identifies the beneficial owner and understands the ownership and control structure, assesses the purpose and intended nature of the relationship and monitors it continuously; identity is verified before the relationship is established (art. 62(1)), subject to the derogations of art. 62(2)-(3). A holding of 25% plus one share, or an ownership interest above 25%, is an 'indication' of beneficial ownership (art. 2(1)). Enhanced due diligence applies to high-risk third countries, cross-border correspondent relationships and politically exposed persons (art. 64). In force on 4 October 2026.167684685686

What the Central Bank of Cyprus (CBC) directive of 2025 fixes

  • Status: K.D.P. 120/2025 (K.D.P. is the Cyprus numbering for regulatory administrative acts), in force since 2 June 2025, binding on credit, electronic money and payment institutions and other CBC-supervised persons.563
  • Natural person (para 30): name as on the identity card or passport, permanent residential address, telephone, e-mail, date and place of birth, occupation with employer and position, and any other information deemed necessary for the assessed risk. Identity is verified on a valid identity card or passport; the address separately, for example by a utility bill or bank statement up to 6 months old.687
  • Company (para 37): certificates of incorporation, registered office, directors and secretary and (private company) shareholders; memorandum and articles; board resolution; nominee trust deeds; ownership structure certified by the beneficial owner; IDs of signatories, shareholders and beneficial owners; shareholder certificates up the ownership chain; recent audited accounts or, failing those, management accounts.688
  • Remote onboarding: the Law accepts electronic identification under Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 or another secure remote process accepted by a competent authority of the Republic (art. 61(1)(a)); the directive requires compliance with EBA Guidelines EBA/GL/2022/15. A relationship started remotely is not high-risk by default: enhanced due diligence applies only where the assessed risk is high (para 27).689690
  • Shell company (para 37): the relationship must be refused or ended where an entity without physical presence in its country of incorporation and/or without established business activity is registered where audited accounts need not be filed and prepares none voluntarily, and/or is tax resident in a jurisdiction on a non-cooperative list, or nowhere.691
  • Remote trading, new in 2025 (para 37(3)-(5)): legal persons that trade remotely may be excluded from the shell definition provided the bank verifies the activity on a risk basis, indicatively through financial statements, tax returns, a business website or online shop.692
  • Registry check: at a new relationship with a company obliged to register its beneficial owners the bank must collect proof of registration or a register extract (Law, art. 62(1) proviso) and may not rely on the register alone; the directive makes it an additional means of verification (para 26(5)). A difference found is reported to the Registrar of Companies (Law, art. 61A(5)(b)) and investigated (para 37(13)).23693

After the relationship starts

  • Periodic review: intervals follow each institution's policy by risk category, with triggers such as a change of directors, shareholders or beneficial owners (para 25); high-risk relationships are updated at least once a year (para 42(7)). Also in the Law and the directive (in force on 4 October 2026)

  • Derogations and failure (Law, art. 62(2)-(4)): verification may be completed during establishment if the risk is low and normal business would otherwise be interrupted; an account may be opened provided no transactions take place until due diligence is complete; if it cannot be completed the entity must not transact or open, must terminate, and considers a report to the financial intelligence unit, MOKAS.167521
  • Economic and risk profile (directive, para 26(11)-(12)): before the relationship starts and before any transaction the bank records, on a separate form, the purpose of the relationship, the anticipated use of products and estimated account volume, the expected source and amount of incoming transfers and destination of outgoing payments, a detailed description of the main activities and the ownership structure.719
  • Form of documents (directive, para 59(1)): seven alternative formats, among them originals; true copies certified by the institution's officer who saw the original or by a relied-on third party; for non-Cypriot citizens and entities incorporated outside Cyprus, originals bearing the Hague 'Apostille'; copies retrieved from the website of the Cyprus Registrar of Companies.720
  • Introduced customers (directive, para 29(4)-(5)): where a third party performed the identification, the bank itself must meet, before any transaction, the natural persons who are beneficial owners, exercise effective control or direct the company's operations; the meeting may be held online with safeguards such as recording; meetings with the introducer or with nominee shareholders do not satisfy the requirement.721
  • Source of funds (directive, para 42(8)(b)(ii)): an enhanced measure institutions 'may' apply is ensuring that source of wealth and source of funds match what the institution knows; where risk is 'particularly high', verifying both 'may be the only appropriate means'. Evidence named, 'inter alia': VAT and income-tax returns, audited accounts, payslips, public documents, independent media.722
  • Client accounts in a third person's name (directive, para 45): enhanced due diligence is mandatory. A pooled one needs sub-accounts or connected accounts and identified beneficial owners of credits of EUR 15,000 or more where the holder is an auditor, accountant, tax adviser, lawyer, trust and company service provider or estate agent from the EEA or a low-risk third country, and of EUR 10,000 or more for others.723
  • Account register (Law, art. 61Δ): CBC-supervised institutions supply, for every IBAN-identified bank or payment account and every safe-deposit box, identification data of the holder and of the beneficial owner, among other data, to a central register kept by the CBC. Who may search it and on what terms, and what is not established about its start, are set out in the section on laws and supervisors.445

Question 7, continued · A founder from outside Cyprus

Non-resident owners: one directive for all, separate bank price lists, country lists and sanctions

The Central Bank of Cyprus (CBC) directive of 2025 has no separate regime for non-resident customers. What differs sits around it: the three large banks' price lists for international clients, the EU list of high-risk third countries (26 jurisdictions on 4 October 2026, Russia since 29 January 2026) and the EU sanctions on Russian and Belarusian clients.

What the CBC directive of 2025 says (K.D.P. 120/2025, in force since 2 June 2025)

SubjectRuleParagraph and detail
No separate regimeThe same data and documents apply to every natural person; foreign companies supply 'corresponding' documents. Residence appears as a categorisation factor ('country of origin and/or residence') and as a trigger for enhanced measures where the customer or its beneficial owner resides in a high-risk third country.30; 37(11); 12(6); 50(3)-(4)704
Remote onboardingA relationship started 'remotely (without the physical presence of the parties)' is not high-risk by default: the institution must assess whether it creates an increased risk and adapt its measures if so. Enhanced due diligence applies only where that risk is high. Electronic identification means do not create an increased risk.27(1)(b); 27(2); 27(4), in particular where the means give a high level of assurance under Regulation (EU) No 910/2014. Institutions must comply with EBA Guidelines EBA/GL/2022/15 on remote customer onboarding (27-28, 59(1)(g))689690
Identity documentA valid identity card or passport. The Cyprus 'Residence Permit of a foreign person (plastic identity card)' is accepted only where a payment service provider offers money remittance. A person who reasonably cannot produce those documents may, absent increased risk, be identified on other evidence the institution finds reliable.30(2); 30(3); 31705
Proof of addressA verified permanent address is required; no country is prescribed. It is verified by an officer's visit, a document up to 6 months old (utility bill, home insurance, municipal or income tax document, other government document, bank statement) or double-registered letter.26(6); 30(6)687705
Certified copiesSeven alternative formats; for non-Cypriot citizens and entities incorporated outside Cyprus one of them is originals bearing the Hague 'Apostille'. The formats the 2025 text adds are in the next block.59(1)706720
TranslationIdentification documents in a language other than Greek or English must be accompanied by a Greek or English document stating that it is a faithful translation of the original, dated and signed by the 'duly authorised person' who made it. No sworn or state translator is required by the text.59(3). For example a certified translator, or a member of the institution's staff with suitable training, the language as mother tongue or a university degree in it707
IntroducersA bank may rely only on a 'third person' that is an obliged entity of art. 2A(a)-(d) of Law 188(I)/2007 or another supervised institution in the EEA or a third country applying equivalent due diligence, not on one established in a high-risk third country. Reliance is allowed only when the relationship is established.Law art. 67(2): branches and subsidiaries of EU obliged entities may be exempted from the high-risk-country bar; 29(1). The bank itself must meet the customer before any transaction; the meeting may be held online with safeguards such as recording (29(4))708721
Client accounts'Client accounts' in a third person's name are a mandatory enhanced-due-diligence category. A pooled account needs sub-accounts or connected accounts and identified beneficial owners of credits of EUR 15,000 or more where the holder is a listed professional, and of EUR 10,000 or more for other holders managing clients' money.42(2)(b); 45(9)-(13). Listed: auditor, accountant, tax adviser, lawyer, trust and company service provider or estate agent from the EEA or a low-risk third country723
Source of fundsAn enhanced measure institutions 'may' apply (not all in every case) is ensuring that the customer's funds are not proceeds of crime and that source of wealth and of funds match what it knows; where risk is 'particularly high', verifying both 'may be the only appropriate means'.42(8)(b)(ii); 42(6). Evidence named, 'inter alia': VAT and income-tax returns, audited accounts, payslips, public documents, independent media722

Under Law 188(I)/2007 a 'high-risk third country' is a country on the EU list 'and a third country which obliged entities classify as high-risk' in their own risk assessment; the CBC directive adds countries under a FATF call for action (para 50(1)). A relationship 'relates to' such a country if the funds were generated in, are received from or are destined for one, if the customer is resident or established there, or if a trustee is established there or the trust is governed by its law. The enhanced measures of art. 64(1)(a) then apply, as they do where the customer's beneficial owner resides there, and the bank may not rely on an introducer established there.556557

Cyprus sanctions laws of 25 July 2025 and the implementation unit

  • Law 149(I)/2025 (25 July 2025) criminalises violations of Union restrictive measures, applies from publication and repealed Law 58(I)/2016. Natural persons face at most five years' imprisonment and/or a fine of up to EUR 100,000 (for most offences the tier requires funds worth at least EUR 100,000); legal persons a fine of up to 1% or 5%, by offence, of worldwide turnover in the financial year before the offence.544
  • Law 150(I)/2025 (both laws: Official Gazette no. 5050, 25 July 2025) set up the National Sanctions Implementation Unit in the Ministry of Finance and makes sanctions compliance a supervised duty of every AML obliged entity: policies, controls and systems, and passing to the Unit any information on a possible breach. The supervisory authority may fine up to EUR 500,000 plus up to EUR 500 a day.543545
  • The CBC's sanctions rulebook on 4 October 2026 is still its directive of March 2020 (First Edition), issued under the repealed Law 58(I)/2016 and kept in force by s. 37(3) of Law 150(I)/2025 until replaced. It requires screening of new customers and related parties (directors, beneficial owners, signatories, nominees, trustees) before any service or transaction.546
  • The Unit's website (launched 14 May 2026; read 4-5 October 2026) carries the three laws of 25 July 2025 in Greek only, a FAQ posted 8 September 2025, an online licence-application service and a note 'Reporting/Disclosure Obligations to the NSIU' (posted 24 April 2026): information on funds of designated persons is due within two weeks. Its reporting templates, two of them for art. 5r, 'are due to be revised shortly'.543736738

Question 8 · Registration, audit, people to hire

The Registrar charges €165 to register a company; an advocate and a statutory auditor are required

As of 4 Oct 2026 the Registrar charges €165 to register a company with share capital; the advocates' stamp is €40 for capital up to €2,000. An advocate must draft the memorandum and articles; a statutory auditor must audit or review the accounts. Review limits: €300,000 net turnover (per ICPAC, periods beginning from 6 February 2026), €500,000 total assets.

By statute the lawyer bears the advocates' stamp: s. 29(1) of the Advocates Law (Cap. 2) forbids an advocate to charge to or collect from any client any amount he paid as fees under s. 27(1). Every private limited liability company must submit its financial statements to audit by statutory auditors or audit firms (Companies Law, Cap. 113, s. 152A(1)(a); since Law 97(I)/2016, for statements ending on 31 December 2016 or later). As of 4 October 2026 the Law has no size-based exemption from external examination; the only relief is a review in place of the audit.55

Audit or review: who qualifies, and since when

SinceWasNowAct
1 Jan 2023Audit for every private limited company.A private limited company may have its financial statements reviewed under ISRE 2400 by a statutory auditor or audit firm instead of audited, provided net turnover and total assets stay within €200,000 and €500,000 for at least two consecutive financial years; applies to periods ending on 31 December 2022 or later. Turnover for this test includes rents, interest, dividends and royalties.Law 88(I)/2022 (Gazette No. 4897, 24.6.2022)5556
6 Feb 2026Net-turnover limit of €200,000.€300,000; the total-assets limit stays at €500,000. The Institute of Certified Public Accountants of Cyprus (ICPAC), in Technical Circular 2/2026, applies the new limit to reporting periods beginning on or after 6 February 2026. Closed to parent companies that must prepare consolidated statements and their subsidiaries, to groups exceeding the limits, and to companies supervised by the Central Bank of Cyprus, the Superintendent of Insurance or the Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission (CySEC) and holders of qualifying holdings in them.Law 2(I)/2026, art. 5 (Gazette No. 5071, 6.2.2026), in force on publication642643
Source trap

The €300,000 net-turnover limit has been in force since 6 February 2026, yet on ICPAC's reading it does not reach calendar year 2026. Law 2(I)/2026 has no transitional clause. ICPAC's Technical Circular 2/2026 (19 February 2026) applies the limit to reporting periods beginning on or after 6 February 2026 and tests earlier ones against €200,000: for a calendar-year company the first financial year under the new limit is 2027. This is the professional body's reading, not a ruling of the Registrar or a court.642643

ICPAC's Technical Circular 2/2026 (19 February 2026) applies the two-consecutive-years test year by year, each year against the turnover limit in force for that year. Its example 3: a company with net turnover of €150,000 in the year ended 31 December 2026 (old €200,000 limit) and €250,000 in the year ended 31 December 2027 (new €300,000 limit), total assets €400,000 in both, is eligible for a review for 2027. Its example 1: €250,000 in each of the years ended 28 February 2025, 2026 and 2027 is not eligible for the year to February 2027, because the earlier year exceeded the €200,000 then applicable.768

Open look again by 4 Apr 2027

A new company's first years are not settled by any public official text found as of 4 Oct 2026. Section 152A(1)(d) requires the limits to be met for at least two consecutive financial years. ICPAC's TC 2/2026 repeats this, has no first-period example and refers to TC 5/2022 'Guide to Review Engagements', whose link leads to the members' login. The one explicit statement found is a provider's (Savva Cyprus, 14 July 2026): a full audit for the first two periods. Tax Department guidance was not searched.769770

As of 4 October 2026 the cylaw consolidated text of the Companies Law is not a safe guide to what is in force. 2013–2026 · What changed and when

2013 to 2026 and the dates already fixed: what circulates is often not the date of effect

Two session notes describe one pattern: the date in circulation - an announcement, a vote, a Gazette date, a recommendation - is often not the date of effect. Events carry the date of effect where a record gives one; the text says which. Entries after 5 October 2026 are dates fixed in or derived from adopted acts, scheme rules, notices or official pages.

2013

26 Mar 2013
Banks
Insured Laiki deposits go to Bank of Cyprus, whose large deposits are bailed in Laiki's insured deposits up to €100,000 moved to Bank of Cyprus as of 26 March 2013. At Bank of Cyprus the bail-in base was deposits above €100,000 net of the customer's loans there. A 37.5% conversion into shares was announced on 30 March 2013; the final rate, fixed on 30 July 2013, was 47.5%.788789

Beneficial-owner register starts under Directive K.D.P. 112/2021 The Registrar's directive is in force from publication on 12 March 2021; the Registrar announced that e-filing would be available on 16 March. Existing entities got six months to file, new ones 30 days from incorporation. The final system replaced this interim one on 14 November 2023.2164791
18 Jun 2021
Payments
Decree K.D.P. 259/2021 lists who must accept cards Published 18 June 2021 (cylaw's index: 28 June); listed payees got three months - per the Tax Department, existing businesses to 18 September 2021. 1 Jul 2021
Tax
EU threshold of EUR 10,000 for cross-border consumer sales applies Art. 59c of Directive 2006/112/EC: a supplier established in only one Member State taxes intra-EU distance sales of goods and telecom, broadcasting and electronic services to consumers at home while their total stays within EUR 10,000 net of VAT in the current and the preceding calendar year.462
13 Sep 2021
Company law
Employers register and notify hires one day ahead, electronically K.D.P. 167/2017, brought into force by K.D.P. 378/2021: an employer applies to register no later than one day before it expects to become an employer (before: within one month of becoming one) and notifies each hiring no later than one day before it, only electronically (Ergani, per the Ministry).161719
15 Oct 2021
Residence and work
Digital Nomad Visa decided, with a ceiling of 100 A residence permit, not a work permit, for non-EU, non-EEA nationals working remotely for an employer or clients abroad. A Council of Ministers decision of 3 March 2022 set the ceiling at 500; it was exhausted by early 2024. On 26 March 2025 applications were announced as accepted.146

2022

2 Jan 2022
Residence and work
Strategy for companies of foreign interests enters into force Approved by the Council of Ministers on 15 October 2021. Per the Migration Department's page on 5 October 2026, 'highly paid' third-country staff need at least €2,500 gross a month, academic qualifications or two years' experience and a contract of at least two years; no quota or labour-market test.129

AML and sanctions
Sanctions: Russian clients' deposits limited (Regulation 833/2014, art. 5b) Inserted by Regulation (EU) 2022/328; wording of Regulation (EU) 2022/1269: no deposits from Russian nationals, residents of Russia, entities established there or non-EU entities they own over 50%, above EUR 100,000 in total per bank. AML and sanctions
Sanctions: accounting, audit and consulting for Russian entities banned Art. 5n of Regulation 833/2014 bans accounting, auditing, bookkeeping, tax consulting and business and management consulting to the Government of Russia or entities established there from 4 June 2022, legal advice from 7 October 2022. Payments

Public access to the beneficial-owner register suspended From 1 June 2022 the general public could obtain a report for a fixed fee of €3.50 per company. Banks stop charging companies for euro deposits Eurobank Cyprus announced the end of negative rates on legal entities' euro deposits from 1 October 2022. Payments
JCC Payment Systems licensed as an electronic money institution The Central Bank of Cyprus register (file dated 28 September 2026) gives JCC's EMI licence date as 12 December 2022, after an original payment-institution licence of 23 April 2010 and a subsequent one of 13 July 2018. Companies of foreign interests must again prove a €200,000 investment A Council of Ministers decision of 30 November 2022, in force 12 December 2022, brought back proof of an initial investment of at least €200,000: on the Business Facilitation Unit's page archived 6 December 2022 in the two shareholding cases only, on its page of 23 September 2026 'in all the cases'.153154

Banks
ECB announces the withdrawal of RCB Bank's licence On 24 March 2022 the ECB announced decisions on RCB's voluntary phase-out of banking operations, with full repayment of depositors. Tax
Incorporation test added to corporate tax residency Before, the only test was management and control in Cyprus. 1 Jan 2023
Company law
Review instead of audit allowed within set limits Law 88(I)/2022 (Gazette of 24 June 2022), applying to periods ending on 31 December 2022 or later: a private limited company may have its statements reviewed under ISRE 2400 if net turnover stays within €200,000 and total assets within €500,000 for at least two consecutive financial years.56
12 Apr 2023
AML and sanctions
US and UK sanctions reach Cyprus-linked persons and firms The US Treasury's OFAC notice of that day lists 34 individuals and 91 entities, 16 and 18 of them with a Cyprus address, nationality or passport (verifier's count); its release has a section 'Usmanov's Cyprus Network'. Bank of Cyprus's third-edition account agreement takes effect Announced by letter of 21 February 2023, silence deemed acceptance. Residence and work
Investor immigration permit: fourth revision of the criteria in force A published policy under Regulation 6(2) of the Aliens and Immigration Regulations, not a law: €300,000 invested and €50,000 annual income. Payments
Law 36(I)/2023 puts the surcharge ban above the duty to disclose charges It made art. 60(1) of Law 31(I)/2018 subject to art. 62(5). AML and sanctions
Central Bank sets out its record after media reports The Central Bank's statement of 16 November 2023 says credit institutions had, since end-2018, ended relationships with 42,728 shell companies and closed 125,782 accounts. 1 Jan 2024
Company law
The €350 annual company levy is abolished Law 25(I)/2024, published 15 March 2024, deletes section 391 of the Companies Law and is deemed in force from 1 January 2024. Tax
Payment providers start recording cross-border payments for tax (CESOP) From 1 January 2024 (Directive (EU) 2020/284) payment service providers keep quarterly records once they provide more than 25 cross-border payments to one payee in a quarter. 1 Jan 2024
Tax
Defence contribution on interest falls from 30% to 17% Law 157(I)/2023 (Gazette of 20 December 2023) set 17% from 1 January 2024. AML and sanctions
Beneficial-owner filing periods lengthened (K.D.P. 34/2024) K.D.P. 34/2024 (Gazette of 29 January 2024) set 90 days from incorporation for a new company's filing, 45 days for recording a change and a yearly confirmation between 1 October and 31 December, replacing 30 days, 14 days and a 1-31 December window. Company law
Late charge on the annual return capped at €150 Law 18(I)/2024: €50 plus €1 a day, capped at €150 per breach. AML and sanctions

Banks
Eurobank takes control of Hellenic Bank After regulatory approvals Eurobank S.A. bought a further 26.1% of Hellenic Bank, lifting its direct holding from 29.20% to 55.3%, and on 4 June 2024 announced a mandatory takeover bid at €2.56 per share. 3 June is the date control passed; the earlier share-purchase agreements were not completion.813

Payments

Payments

Payments

25% income tax relief of art. 8(21B), in force by retroactive commencement Law 17(I)/2026 (Gazette 6 March 2026), deemed in force 1 January 2025: 25% of an individual's employment pay or business profits in Cyprus is exempt up to €25,000 a year. Payments

Payments

Payments

Sanctions: no payment services for Russian clients (Regulation (EU) 2025/2033) Art. 5b(2) of Regulation (EU) No 833/2014 as replaced: no acquiring, issuing of payment instruments or e-money, payment initiation or crypto-asset services for Russian nationals, residents of Russia and entities established there. Banks

Payments
PSD3 and Payment Services Regulation: provisional agreement only A provisional agreement is not adoption. The proposals date from 28 June 2023; ECON approved the agreed text on 5 May 2026. 1 Jan 2026
Tax
The 2026 tax reform takes effect Six tax laws published on 31 December 2025 took effect, a few provisions later: corporate tax 15% (12.5% before); special defence contribution on dividends of resident-and-domiciled individuals 5% (17% on pre-2026 profits of Cyprus-resident companies); deemed distribution ends for profits from 2026.460610611613

Payments
Fine ceiling under the card-acceptance decree rises to EUR 6,000 Law 243(I)/2025, Article 32, raised the administrative fine under Article 50ΣΤ of Law 4/1978 to up to EUR 6,000. 1 Jan 2026
Company law
State stamp duty repealed Law 239(I)/2025 repealed the Stamp Duty Laws; the Registrar announced on 19 January 2026 that documents submitted to it need no stamp duty as of 1 January 2026. Documents signed by at least one party up to 31 December 2025 remain subject to it. The Bar Association stamp on form HE1 is separate.293744
1 Jan 2026
Tax
Tax Commissioner may seal a business that issues no receipts Art. 32A of Law 4/1978, added by Law 243(I)/2025: a business may be suspended and sealed for up to ten days, after three notices, where its operator did not issue the invoices or receipts the Law requires, among other grounds. Refusing cards is not one; it stays under the fine of Article 50ΣΤ.495497
1 Jan 2026
Tax
17% on dividends to low-tax jurisdictions never took effect; 5% applies Law 48(I)/2025 (16 April 2025) extended the 17% charge on dividends to connected companies in EU-listed non-cooperative jurisdictions to low-tax jurisdictions, that part only from 1 January 2026. On that day Law 245(I)/2025 set 5% for low-tax jurisdictions, keeping 17% for non-cooperative ones.663664
1 Jan 2026
Residence and work
National minimum wage rises to €1,088 a month Decree K.D.P. 427/2025: €1,088 a month for full-time employment, €979 for an employee who has not completed six months of continuous employment with the same employer. Earlier steps under the Minimum Wage Decree of 2022 (in force 1 January 2023): €940 and €885; from 1 January 2024, €1,000 and €900.95
1 Jan 2026
Tax
Individuals' duty to register for a tax number: s. 5A(1A) in force Law 4/1978, s. 5A(1A), inserted by Law 243(I)/2025: an individual resident in Cyprus who has reached 25, or has income under art. 5 of the Income Tax Law, gives notice and obtains a tax number; no period is stated. A proviso gives one without such income in 2026 and 2027 until 31 December 2027.99

Banks
Alpha Bank Cyprus reprices company current accounts From 19 January 2026: €80 quarterly per current account without limit, small companies in a separate catalogue; the 7 May 2025 edition charged small organisations €60, SME and corporate €100. AML and sanctions
Russia and the British Virgin Islands join the EU high-risk list Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/46 added a point IV with the Russian Federation as its only entry; 2026/83 added Bolivia and the British Virgin Islands and removed Burkina Faso, Mali, Mozambique, Nigeria, South Africa and Tanzania. Migration Department notice on contracts after the end of stamp duty Greek-only notice: a document drawn up and signed, even by one party, after 01/01/2026 is not subject to stamp duty; documents signed up to 31/12/2025 are stamped as before. Company law

Residence and work
Investor permit: filing on the 2021 criteria ends The Migration Department ended, 'with immediate effect', the transitional arrangement announced on 29 August 2023 under which an application under Regulation 6(2) could still be filed on the Third Revision (24 March 2021). 20 Mar 2026
AML and sanctions
Register access moves to a legitimate-interest test Law 25(I)/2026 (no commencement clause) replaced 'a member of the general public' in s. 61A(6)(α)(iii) of the AML Law with persons proving a legitimate interest, eight months after the 10 July 2025 deadline of art. 74 of Directive (EU) 2024/1640. 2 Apr 2026
Payments
Existing account elsewhere no longer a ground to refuse a basic account Law 41(I)/2026 replaced art. 17(9) of Law 64(I)/2017: a bank may no longer refuse a payment account with basic features because the consumer already holds a payment account with another credit institution in Cyprus. 19 Jun 2026

Online renewal of residence permits through CY Login The Migration Department launched online renewal through a verified CY Login profile - renewals, 'not initial applications' - for five categories, including long-term residents and, with the same employer only, employees of companies of foreign interests. Payments
Pre-application stage for payment and e-money licences By announcement of 31 July 2026 the Central Bank of Cyprus introduced a pre-application exploratory stage with a non-refundable €5,000 fee and a preliminary assessment within 30 working days (50 if an enhanced due-diligence report is requested). Tax
Temporary zero VAT on basic goods continues K.D.P. 354/2026, as announced by the Tax Department on 2 October 2026: zero rate to 31 May 2027 on fresh, chilled or frozen meat and fish from 1 October 2026 and on bread, milk, coffee, sugar and baby food from 12 October. Payments

Payments

Payments

Law 59(I)/2010 lists as insurable employment of an employed person the 'employment of a person under any circumstances in a private company in which he is a shareholder' (First Schedule, Part I, para 5). Contributions are due 'except where the earnings of the employed person are negligible' - below €2 a week or €7 a month (reg. 7, K.D.P. 289/2010); no minimum insurable earnings are set for him. 5 Apr 2027Founder's pathA sole shareholder-director as 'employee': minimum wage and written terms
Do the Minimum Wage Decree and Law 25(I)/2023 on written terms of employment apply to a sole shareholder-director employed by his own company?		The Minimum Wage Decree (K.D.P. 350/2022) has no exception and no rule for directors or shareholders: it applies to 'all employees in the Republic', an employee working for another under a contract or relationship of employment, or in circumstances from which one can be inferred; whether a sole shareholder-director is an 'employee' is not addressed. Law 25(I)/2023 applies to 'all employees' except those working on average up to three hours a week; 'employee' turns on an employment relationship, 'taking into account the case law of the Court of Justice', and no exception for directors is named.9697Guidance of the Department of Labour Relations, or Cyprus case law on whether a controlling shareholder-director is an employee; for a third-country national, the salary terms attached to the employment permit.Looked: K.D.P. 350/2022 as amended by K.D.P. 427/2025 (read in full); Law 25(I)/2023 arts 2, 4, 11 and 12. Guidance of the Department of Labour Relations on directors was not searched beyond these texts.
5 Apr 2027Founder's pathGeSY for a founder outside plain employment
Is an EU citizen who lives on dividends from his own Cyprus company a 'self-employed worker' for the General Healthcare System (GeSY), which residence permits of third-country nationals carry the right to equal treatment in social security, and where does a visitor-permit holder stand?		Art. 16(1) of Law 89(I)/2001 (5 October 2026) lists as beneficiaries, among others and if ordinarily resident in the government-controlled areas, a Union citizen who is an employed or self-employed worker in Cyprus, retains that status or holds permanent residence, and a third-country national with a lawful right of permanent residence or of equal treatment in the branches of social security under the Aliens and Immigration Law. 5 Apr 2027Non-residentsA non-resident director's fee

Art. 5(2)(β) of the Income Tax Law, as replaced by Law 244(I)/2025 (in force 1 January 2026), taxes a non-resident on income from 'any office or employment exercised in the Republic'. On 4 October 2026 Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 is in force, unamended; it applies from 10 July 2027, with a beneficial-owner test of '25 % or more' against '25% plus one share' or 'more than 25%' in Cyprus law. 31 Dec 2031TaxesTransitional dividend rules after the 2026 reform
Until when do the 17% rate on dividends from pre-2026 profits and the deemed distribution of 2024 and 2025 profits apply?		In force on 4 October 2026. Dividends received from a Cyprus-resident company within six years of 1 January 2026 (the Tax Department writes 'until 31/12/2031') and paid out of profits of tax years up to and including 2025 still bear 17%. A Cyprus-resident company is deemed to have distributed 70% of its after-tax accounting profits of tax years 2024 and 2025 at the end of two years from the end of the year of the profits, with 17% charged only for profits attributable to individuals resident and domiciled in Cyprus at the deemed-distribution date.611613Any amending law before the end dates; Tax Department guidance on the transitional provisos.Looked: Law 245(I)/2025 arts. 3 and 4; Tax Department presentation of 6 March 2026.
Method · How this page was built

Read in the primary document, attacked by a second reader, stored word for word

The page is a view of 879 memory records gathered in three rounds. Each record is one checked statement with its source, and the page says nothing that a record does not carry.

What adversarial checking did to the 313 researcher facts

Each of six research slices was read again by two verifiers whose task was to refute it.

Confirmed as written — 109 (34.8%) Corrected: qualifier, status, date, act or scope — 204 (65.2%) Refuted — 0 (0.0%)

The verifiers also added 79 facts of their own. 49 records that repeated another slice were dropped and two session notes were added, which leaves 345.

The second round: what adversarial checking did to its 330 researcher facts

Eight slices on what the first round left open, each read again by two verifiers whose task was to refute it.

Confirmed as written — 128 (38.8%) Corrected: qualifier, status, date, act or scope — 200 (60.6%) Refuted — 0 (0.0%) Repeated a first-round record — 2 (0.6%)

The verifiers added 66 facts of their own, one of them twice. With twelve corrected editions of first-round records that makes 405 records stored in the second round.

The third round: what adversarial checking did to its 105 researcher facts

Three slices on the founder who lives in Cyprus and is not a citizen, each read again by two verifiers whose task was to refute it.

Confirmed as written — 30 (28.6%) Corrected: group covered, instrument, status, date or scope — 74 (70.5%) Refuted — 0 (0.0%) Repeated a fact of another slice — 1 (1.0%)

The verifiers added 40 facts of their own, three of them repeating a fact of another slice or of the other verifier. That makes 141 records stored in the third round; no earlier record had to be retired.

Distance to the source, 879 records

Channel class of each record: where the statement was read.

Primary document — 773 (87.9%) Archived snapshot of it — 69 (7.8%) Press — 11 (1.3%) Session outline — 26 (3.0%)

Numbers: 394 records carry a number fixed by the act or price list itself, 96 a number counted by this study with the method stated, 24 a number whose origin the document does not explain, 365 no number.

Order of work. Memory was asked first: eight narrow questions returned fifteen earlier records on EU licence capital, interchange caps and scheme rules, and nothing on Cyprus company formation, bank onboarding, merchant agreements, Cyprus taxes or provider terms. Six researchers then read laws, the Official Gazette, regulator pages, scheme rulebooks, provider terms and price lists on 4 October 2026. Two verifiers per slice reopened every cited document.

What the verifiers corrected. Four kinds of error account for most of the 204 corrections: a rule dated by its enactment when a later act had changed it (the card-acceptance fine, the beneficial-owner deadlines); a rule attributed to the instrument that restates it instead of the one that introduced it; a qualifier lost in paraphrase ("may be requested", "where available", a second limb of an exemption); and a negative established by looking in one place. Guidance pages of the Registrar and the consolidated texts on cylaw.org were the most frequent source of the first kind: the consolidation prints provisions that are not yet in force.

The second round. The first page listed 40 questions it could not answer. On 4 and 5 October 2026 memory was asked again — eight questions, seven answered in part and one not at all, every record returned belonging to the first round — and eight researchers went back to the web for the rest: the bank and provider contracts and their earlier versions in the Internet Archive, who acquires in Cyprus, registry fees and deadlines, tax points, the non-resident founder, year-by-year counts, scheme and PCI rules. Sixteen verifiers corrected 200 of 330 facts, again for scope and time. Twelve first-round records turned out to hold a clause the new documents contradict; each was replaced by a corrected edition and the old text was retired, not deleted.

The third round. On 5 October 2026 the reader asked what a founder who lives in Cyprus and is not a citizen has to obtain, in which order, where and when. Memory was asked three questions: the company's path, its deadlines and the founder's tax position were there; nothing on residence status, the founder's own registrations or processing times. Three researchers read the immigration law and regulations, the Migration Department's forms and document lists, the tax, social insurance and health-system pages, and read the order of steps again as it stood that day. Six verifiers corrected 74 of 105 facts — most often a rule stated for the wrong group, or a page's wording given as the law's — and listed the steps of the researchers' sequences that no document supports; the page shows those as not established. Nothing in the earlier records had to be retired.

From records to page. After each round the stored text, tags and source of every record were compared with the prepared files byte by byte: no differences in 345, in 405 and in 141 records. The first page was written from the records by five writers without web access and checked item by item by five checkers: of 425 items 89 were corrected and 32 added. For the second round seven writers changed or wrote 654 items — five updated the existing sections, two wrote four new ones — and seven checkers corrected 111 of them, dropped 11 and added 12. For the third round five writers changed or wrote 155 items — one wrote the two sections on the founder, four updated existing ones — and five checkers corrected 57 of them and added 14. The typical fault was the same each time: compressing a record to fit a table cell cuts off the clause that bounds it, so a negative reads wider than what was looked at, a rule reads as timeless, or a page's wording reads as the law's. The appendix prints all 879 records, those that no section cites included.

Limits. This is a reference study, not legal, immigration or tax advice. Walk-throughs and tax outlines are assembled from the records and compute nothing: no effective rate, no total cost. Market prices for formation and accounting are what firms advertise. A register row for a passported institution is a notification, not evidence that it serves merchants in Cyprus. Cyprus legislation has no machine resolver, so act numbers rest on the Gazette and cylaw.org as read.

Provisional tax in Cyprus: a person with income other than emoluments submits its own estimate of the year's chargeable income before 31 July of the tax year (art. 24 of Law 4/1978) and pays in two instalments — the Tax Department's deadline calendar for 2026 lists 31 July and 31 December. The estimate can be revised until 31 December. If the provisional chargeable income is below three quarters of the final figure, an additional tax of one tenth of the difference between final tax and provisional tax is due (art. 26(1)). It is set by the Minimum Wage Decree of 2022 (K.D.P. 350/2022, made under s. 3(1) of the Minimum Wage Law, Cap. 183, in force 1 January 2023), para 5 as replaced by the amending Decree K.D.P. 427/2025 (Gazette No. 5989, 31 December 2025) with effect from 1 January 2026. Earlier steps: €940 and €885 from 1 January 2023; €1,000 and €900 from 1 January 2024 (K.D.P. 402/2023, repealed by the 2025 decree). Part-time pay is adjusted in proportion to hours.Official Gazette of the Republic of Cyprus (cylaw copy) · K.D.P. 427/2025 paras 3-5, K.D.P. 350/2022 paras 5 and 12 · edition: K.D.P. 427/2025 as published, K.D.P. 350/2022 (Gazette No. 5737, 2.9.2022) as published, K.D.P. 402/2023 (Gazette No. 58 · K.D.P. 350/2022, K.D.P. 427/2025, Minimum Wage Law, Cap. 183, s. 3(1) · read 2026-10-05 · channel: primary · memory 973808ae · cylaw.org · cylaw.org
  96. Cyprus's Minimum Wage Decree has no exception and no rule for directors or shareholders. K.D.P. 350/2022 applies to 'all employees in the Republic' (para 3(1)); an employee is a person working for another under a contract or relationship of employment or apprenticeship, or in circumstances from which an employer-employee relationship can be inferred (para 2). Outside it (3(2)-(5)): domestic, farm and livestock workers, seafarers; workers under more favourable arrangements; hotel staff under their own decree; trainees for a diploma or profession. 'Minimum monthly wage' means total gross monthly insurable earnings in money. Whether a sole shareholder-director is an 'employee' is not addressed.Official Gazette of the Republic of Cyprus (cylaw copy) · K.D.P. 350/2022 para 2 (definitions of «εργοδοτούμενος», «κατώτατος μηνιαίος μισθός»), para 3(1)-(5) · edition: K.D.P. 350/2022 as published (Gazette No. 5737, 2.9.2022), para 3(4) amended by K.D.P. 427/2025 para 2 · K.D.P. 350/2022, paras 2-3 · read 2026-10-05 · channel: primary · memory 74a20520 · cylaw.org
  97. A Cyprus company owes a director a written statement of terms if he is its employee. Law 25(I)/2023 on Transparent and Predictable Working Conditions (transposing Directive (EU) 2019/1152) applies to 'all employees' except those working on average up to three hours a week; seafarers and fishermen are covered with carve-outs (art. 4). 'Employee' (art. 3) turns on an employment relationship, 'taking into account the case law of the Court of Justice'. The employer gives the basic terms (parties, place, job, start date, pay, working time and others) on paper or electronically within seven calendar days of the start, the rest within one month (arts 11-12). No exception for directors is named.CyLaw (Cyprus Bar Association) - consolidated legislation · Law 25(I)/2023, art. 3 definition of «εργοδοτούμενος», art. 4(α)-(γ), art. 11(1)-(3), art. 12(1)-(2) · edition: cylaw consolidated text read 2026-10-05, amended by Laws 85(I)/2024 and 126(I)/2024, no amending law in cylaw's 2025-202 · Law 25(I)/2023, arts 3, 4, 11, 12, Directive (EU) 2019/1152 = CELEX 32019L1152 · read 2026-10-05 · channel: primary · memory b323e21d · cylaw.org

  99. Cyprus law gives an individual no day-count deadline for tax registration. Section 5A(1A) of the Assessment and Collection of Taxes Law 4/1978, inserted by art. 5 of Law 243(I)/2025 (in force 1 January 2026), obliges an individual to give notice for registration and obtain a TIN where he is resident in Cyprus and has reached the age of 25, or has income falling under art. 5 of the Income Tax Law; unlike s. 5A(2) for companies (60 days) it states no period.   206. Cyprus tax law says with whom a merchant may contract for card acceptance. Art. 30A(2) of Law 4/1978 (in force since 20 August 2020): to accept card payment instruments, payees contract with lawfully licensed payment service providers within the meaning of the Payment Services Law 31(I)/2018; the proviso forbids payees, for card acceptance and for collection on behalf of a third party generally, to contract with entities that are not lawfully licensed payment service providers or their agents, unless legislation expressly provides otherwise. Decree K.D.P. 259/2021 repeats the rule, and breaches of the decree are finable under art. 50ΣΤ.   271. A Cyprus merchant may not surcharge card payments. Unchanged: two months' notice of contract changes (art. 42(1) of 2009; art. 54(1) of 2018), two months' notice of termination by the provider (art. 43(3); art. 55(3)), and a user notice period of not more than one month. Visa's public rules (edition 18 April 2026) put wallets that hand the card credential to the merchant - the model of Apple Pay and Google Pay - in their own class, 'Pass-Through Digital Wallet', outside the 'Digital Wallet Operator' class. The glossary defines it as functionality of a non-issuer that is usable at more than one merchant, stores a payment credential and transfers it directly to the merchant, after which the merchant 'finalizes the Transaction with its Acquirer, and the Pass-Through Digital Wallet is not involved in the Authorization, Clearing, or Settlement payment flow'. A Digital Wallet Operator is one operating a staged or stored-value wallet. Visa names no wallet brand.Visa · Glossary 'Pass-Through Digital Wallet' (ID# 0029533, PDF pp. 881-882), glossary 'Digital Wallet Operator (DWO)' (ID# 0029530, p. 854), section 4.1.18.1 (ID# 002 · edition: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules, 18 April 2026 (public) · Visa Rules ID# 0029533, ID# 0029530, ID# 0029534 · read 2026-10-04 · channel: primary · memory af4e7d43 · usa.visa.com

  408. Since 24 October 2025 EU sanctions bar payment services for Russian clients. Regulation (EU) 2025/2033 replaced art. 5b(2) of Regulation (EU) No 833/2014, prohibiting the provision of crypto-asset services, issuing of payment instruments, acquiring of payment transactions, payment initiation services and issuing of electronic money to Russian nationals, natural persons residing in Russia and entities established in Russia. Nationals of, and residence-permit holders in, an EU or EEA state or Switzerland are exempt (art. 5b(3)); authorities may authorise exceptions (arts. 5c, 5d). Art. 61Δ of Cyprus Law 188(I)/2007 (in force 4 October 2026) is silent on telling an account holder that the Central Register of Bank Accounts was searched: no duty to notify and, unlike arts. 61A(7) and 61B(7) on the beneficial-owner registers, no 'without notification' clause. Its safeguard is a log: the Central Bank records every access (date and time, data used, authority, user), has it checked by its data protection officer, gives it to the data protection Commissioner on request and deletes entries after five years unless an audit is under way (61Δ(5), added by Law 40(I)/2022).   490. A VAT-registered shop or café in Cyprus must hand every consumer a 'legal receipt' at the time of sale.   492. For a shop, the commission kept by the card company does not reduce the VAT base. In Chaussures Bally (C-18/92, judgment of 25 May 1993) the Court of Justice held, on art. 11A(1)(a) of the Sixth VAT Directive (now art. 73 of Directive 2006/112/EC), that where the purchaser pays by credit card and the card-issuing organisation pays the supplier the price after deducting a percentage as commission for the service it renders to the supplier, the sum so deducted must be included in the taxable amount on which the supplier pays VAT.   494. Article 50ΣΤ of Cyprus's Law 4/1978 sets a short procedure for the card-acceptance fine (consolidated text read 5 October 2026). The officer who finds the breach reports to the Tax Commissioner within five working days, and the decision imposing the fine is issued within fifteen working days of the report. The business may object to the Commissioner within 30 days of notification and the Commissioner decides within 30 days; the decision on the objection can be taken to the Administrative Court, and a fine already paid is returned if the objection or the action succeeds. An unpaid fine is recovered as a civil debt. Salary: deductible against the 15% corporate tax; taxed in the director's hands on the 0-35% scale (first €22,000 at 0%); social insurance 8.8% employee plus 8.8% employer up to the insurable ceiling; GeSY 2.65% plus 2.90%; employer-only funds 1.2%, 0.5% and 2% (the 2% Social Cohesion Fund has no earnings ceiling). Dividend: paid out of profit after 15% corporate tax; SDC 5% - or 17% if paid by 31/12/2031 by a Cyprus-resident company out of profits of years up to 2025 - and only if the recipient is resident and domiciled; GeSY 2.65% on the dividend, with all GeSY-liable income capped at €180,000 a year; no social insurance.outline assembled by the session from the records of this page · read 2026-10-04 · channel: inferred · memory 1ae0a9a6

Income tax reliefs for a founder who moves to Cyprus and takes employment there (Income Tax Law 118(I)/2002, art. 8, read on 4 October 2026): (23Α) 50% of remuneration from employment in Cyprus is exempt for a person not resident in Cyprus for at least 15 consecutive years before first employment starting on or after 1 January 2022, for 17 tax years, in any year remuneration exceeds €55,000; (21Α) 20% of remuneration or €8,550, whichever is lower, for seven tax years, for first employment starting up to 2027 after three years' employment abroad by a non-resident employer.   674. Cyprus has a third relief beside the 20% and 50% exemptions. Law 17(I)/2026 (Gazette 6 March 2026, deemed in force 1 January 2025) added art. 8(21B) to Income Tax Law 118(I)/2002: 25% of pay from employment in Cyprus, or of an individual's business profits there, is exempt up to €25,000 a year, in the start year and the six following, each year the income exceeds €30,000. It reaches only a person who starts in 2025-2030, was not resident in the seven tax years before the start year but was resident in an earlier year, and worked full time abroad for a non-resident employer for 84 months, or 36 of the last 84 with a recognised degree.   675. Cyprus's 50% exemption is anchored to the first employment in Cyprus, not to the founder's own company. Art. 8(23A) proviso (iv) of Law 118(I)/2002: 'first employment' starts when a person, after 15 consecutive tax years without any salaried services in Cyprus, begins such services for a resident or non-resident employer. Tax Department Circular 4/2024 (8 July 2024), para 10: whoever performed salaried services in Cyprus, of any duration, in the 15 tax years before is not eligible; para 11: services count when performed with physical presence in Cyprus. The Department's FAQ (updated 6 August 2026) adds that changing employer does not affect eligibility. Art. 8(21A) uses the same definition.Tax Department, Ministry of Finance (Cyprus) · Circular 4/2024, paras 9-11 (pp. 2-3), Law 118(I)/2002, art. 8(23A) proviso (iv) and art. 8(21A) second proviso, FAQ https://www.gov.cy/mof-tax/documents/forolo · edition: Circular 4/2024 dated 8 July 2024 (scan, read from page images), consolidated Law 118(I)/2002 on cylaw read 2026-10-05, · Tax Department Circular 4/2024, Law 118(I)/2002, art. 8(23A) proviso (iv), art. 8(21A) · read 2026-10-05 · channel: primary · memory 222fc84f · gov.cy · cylaw.org
  676. A founder already living in Cyprus when his first employment there starts may fail the residence test of the 50% exemption. Per Tax Department Circular 4/2024 (8 July 2024), paras 13-14, the 15 consecutive years of non-residence are the tax years before the year in which the first employment in Cyprus starts; that year itself is not counted, whether or not the person was resident in it. Its example: a start in 2023 requires non-residence in every year from 2008 to 2022. One earlier year of Cyprus tax residence breaks the chain. The 20% exemption instead requires three consecutive years of employment outside Cyprus for a non-resident employer immediately before (Circular 10/2022, part II).Tax Department, Ministry of Finance (Cyprus) · Circular 4/2024, paras 6(i), 12-14 (pp. 2-3), Circular 10/2022, part II, 'Πεδίο εφαρμογής' (i) (p. 3) · edition: Circular 4/2024 dated 8 July 2024, Circular 10/2022 dated 1 November 2022 (scans, read from page images) · Tax Department Circulars 4/2024 and 10/2022, Law 118(I)/2002, art. 8(23A), 8(21A) · read 2026-10-05 · channel: primary · memory 68daf441 · gov.cy · gov.cy
  677. The Cyprus Tax Department accepts the 50% and 20% first-employment exemptions for a person employed by a company he set up himself, on conditions. For Cyprus's first-employment exemptions the Tax Department does not count 'gain or profit from holding an office' as remuneration from employment (Circular 4/2024, para 11(iii), on art. 8(23A); Circular 10/2022, part I, 1(β)(iii), on arts 8(21A) and 8(23A)). Under art. 60 of Cyprus Law 188(I)/2007 an obliged entity applies customer due diligence when it establishes a business relationship, carries out an occasional transaction of EUR 15,000 or more (single or linked operations) or a transfer of funds above EUR 1,000, suspects money laundering regardless of amount, or doubts earlier identification data. Art. 2(1) of Cyprus Law 188(I)/2007 defines the beneficial owner of a legal person as the natural person who ultimately owns or controls it through a sufficient percentage of shares, voting rights or ownership interest, or by other means; companies listed on a regulated market are excepted. A holding of 25% plus one share, or an ownership interest above 25%, held directly or indirectly, is an 'indication' of ownership. Only if all possible means are exhausted, there are no grounds for suspicion and nobody is identified - or the person identified is in doubt - is the senior managing official treated as beneficial owner.   686. Cyprus Law 188(I)/2007 art. 64 requires enhanced due diligence for business with high-risk third countries, for cross-border correspondent relationships and for politically exposed persons. Cyprus VAT Circular 156 of 11 October 2011 follows the Court of Justice in Nordea (C-350/10): SWIFT services are electronic messaging, cause no legal or financial change between the parties, and are not exempt. Beyond three months the right of residence exists if he or she is an employed or self-employed worker in the Republic, or has sufficient resources and comprehensive sickness insurance cover in the Republic, or is enrolled as a student with such insurance and a declaration of sufficient resources, or is a family member accompanying or joining such a citizen (art. 9(1)(α)-(δ)). The authority may not fix an amount that it regards as sufficient resources and must take the person's own situation into account (art. 10(5)).CyLaw (Cyprus Bar Association) - consolidated legislation · Law 7(I)/2007, arts 8(1), 9(1), 10(5) · edition: CyLaw consolidated text, amendment history 7(I)/2007, 181(I)/2011, 8(I)/2013, 67(I)/2013, 77(I)/2015, 28(I)/2017, 193(I) · Law 7(I)/2007, arts 8-10 · read 2026-10-05 · channel: primary · memory 36f88f46 · cylaw.org

Support staff in a Cyprus company of foreign interests are capped: under the government's Strategy (update of 5 February 2024, action 2) third-country nationals on a gross monthly salary below €2,500 may be employed only if they do not exceed 30% of all support staff and hold an employment contract certified by the competent authority; their pay follows the general legislation. The same text says that to obtain permits for third-country staff a company must produce certificates of registration with the Registrar of Companies and with the Tax Department. Cyprus's Social Insurance Law 59(I)/2010 has no rule for third-country nationals as such (text read 5 October 2026): insurable employment turns on work in Cyprus (First Schedule, Part I, para 1). Part II, para 4 excludes by residence, not nationality: a person not ordinarily resident in Cyprus or another Member State employed by an employer with no residence, seat or place of business in Cyprus. Only the Services' Employer Guide (PDF of 2 June 2025) names them: 'international activities companies' owe contributions for all employees, but third-country employees who prove to the Director, on application, that they are not ordinarily resident in Cyprus are exempted. Joining Cyprus's GeSY is governed by the Health Insurance Organisation's Decisions K.D.P. 164/2019 (Gazette No. 5161, 17 May 2019, under art. 16(5) of Law 89(I)/2001); cylaw's indexes to K.D.P. 372/2026 list no amendment. A non-Cypriot is identified by 'the relevant number issued by the Migration Department' (Annex I). A request meeting Decision 5 is approved automatically; three groups must also send a signed paper request with documents: S1 holders, EU citizens who retain worker or self-employed status (alien registration certificate, proof of ordinary residence and e.g. Labour Department form R 210 (ES19)), and family members.
